Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screenless fitness band similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. As someone who has been using a WHOOP for the past six months, I agree the concept is appealing, but I hope Apple can do a few things better.

Since the product is still at a fairly early stage of development, we don't know much about what Apple's screenless fitness band will look like. It is not expected to launch until 2028 at the earliest. Bloomberg described it as "a slim fabric band with a built-in sensor module."

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase on a promotion that let Chase Sapphire cardholders get a WHOOP band at a discount or for free — that's how I got mine. I've been using it, but never fully committed.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection is never perfect, and having to pull out your phone to log a workout, either before or after, is annoying. With an Apple Watch, you can start tracking a workout right from the watch face, and WHOOP also syncs time data from Apple Health. That's the main reason I still wear an Apple Watch.

Pulling out your phone at the gym is acceptable; but when I'm on a bike ride or going for a walk, I really don't want that hassle.

So for Apple's screenless fitness band, I would love to see some kind of button and indicator light so you can start and stop tracking a workout. You still have to categorize the workout on your phone afterwards, but I'd rather deal with that later than in the moment. Apple could also build a classification model based on certain factors.

Summary

If Apple can develop a screenless fitness band that doesn't rely on a phone and isn't a hassle to use, I think it would be very appealing. There are several advantages to this design, including a more comfortable fit, longer battery life, and the ability to wear it alongside a traditional watch.

TB Featured Comments

I bought a FitBit Air because I got tired of wearing basically only an Apple Watch for the past few years. I like mechanical watches, but I also want to track health data, and I like the convenience a watch brings, like using Apple Pay without pulling out my phone, or using it to open the door when my hands are full. If Apple came out with something similar but fully integrated into its ecosystem — letting me use a stripped-down version of Apple Pay, door keys, car keys and other NFC functions, plus the ability to connect to AirPods so Siri can read notifications or perform actions for me — I'd be first in line to buy one.

Personally, after evaluating WHOOP, I found I still prefer wearing a smartwatch, even if it means sacrificing battery life. I understand some people want a screenless design to avoid distractions, but for me, I usually just put the watch in Do Not Disturb mode.

What are your thoughts on Apple developing a screenless fitness band? How much would it need to cost for you to buy one? Let us know in the comments.
